rules.title: Tenant Protection Act just cause requirement (Civil Code 1946.2)
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner may not terminate the tenancy without just cause, which must be stated in the written notice to terminate. If adult tenants are added before an existing tenant reaches 24 months, the rule applies only if all tenants have 12 months or more or at least one tenant has 24 months or more.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 12 months of continuous and lawful occupancy (or 24 months for one tenant if adult tenants were added)
rules.coverage_text: Residential real property where the tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 12 months (all tenants 12 months or one tenant 24 months where adult tenants were added). Just cause is either at-fault (e.g., nonpayment, material lease breach, nuisance, waste, refusal to renew a similar lease, criminal activity, unlawful subletting, refusal of lawful entry, unlawful use, failure to vacate after employment ends or after tenant's own notice) or no-fault (owner or relative move-in, withdrawal from the rental market, compliance with a government or court order or local ordinance requiring vacating, intent to demolish or substantially remodel). For curable lease violations, notice and an opportunity to cure must be given first.

rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy; housing in nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly or adult residential facilities; dormitories owned and operated by higher education institutions or K-12 schools; housing where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen with an owner who lives there; single-family owner-occupied residences (including where the owner-occupant rents no more than two units or bedrooms, and mobilehomes); a two-unit property in a single structure where the owner occupied one unit at the start of the tenancy and continues in occupancy (neither unit an ADU/JADU); housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless a mobilehome; separately alienable property not owned by a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, where tenants received the required written exemption notice; deed- or agreement-restricted or subsidized affordable housing for very low, low, or moderate income households.
rules.penalty: Failure to comply renders the written termination notice void. An owner who attempts to recover possession in material violation is liable for actual damages, in the court's discretion reasonable attorney's fees and costs, and upon a showing of willfulness, oppression, fraud, or malice up to three times actual damages plus possible punitive damages; the Attorney General and city attorney or county counsel may seek injunctive relief.
rules.quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.interaction_text: Residential real property subject to a local ordinance requiring just cause for termination of a residential tenancy adopted on or before September 1, 2019, in which case the local ordinance shall apply. A residential real property shall not be subject to both a local ordinance requiring just cause for termination of a residential tenancy and this section.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for no-fault just cause terminations (Civil Code 1946.2(d))
rules.requirement: When terminating a tenancy covered by the just cause requirement for a no-fault just cause, the owner must, regardless of the tenant's income, either pay the tenant direct relocation assistance or waive in writing the final month's rent, equal to one month of the tenant's rent in effect when the notice was issued. Relocation assistance must be provided within 15 calendar days of service of the notice, and the termination notice must inform the tenant of this right.
rules.key_value: One month of the tenant's rent in effect when the termination notice was issued
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies for which just cause is required under subdivision (a) that are terminated for a no-fault just cause (owner or relative move-in, withdrawal from the rental market, compliance with a government or court order or local ordinance, demolition or substantial remodel).

rules.exemptions: A tenant found by a government agency or court to be at fault for the condition triggering an order or need to vacate is not entitled to relocation assistance. The section's general exemptions in subdivision (e) also apply.
rules.penalty: An owner's failure to strictly comply with this subdivision renders the notice of termination void.
rules.quoted_span: The amount of relocation assistance or rent waiver shall be equal to one month of the tenant’s rent that was in effect when the owner issued the notice to terminate the tenancy.
rules.interaction_text: The relocation assistance or rent waiver required by this subdivision shall be credited against any other relocation assistance required by any other law.
